items.article_context_en: The draft budget proposal targets EU-regulated electronic money tokens starting in 2027, reversing France's traditional tax-free crypto-to-crypto stance. France’s legislators introduced a new proposal to expand its 31.4% crypto capital gains tax to include trades involving European Union (EU)-regulated stablecoins, a move Chanalysis warns could drive investors toward stablecoins outside the bloc’s rules. The proposal is part of France's 2027 budget, which lawmakers began debating last week in the National Assembly and have until Dec. An amendment adopted by the National Assembly’s finance committee on Oct. 7 would make it a taxable event when investors exchange cryptocurrencies such as bitcoin for stablecoins classified as electronic money tokens under the EU’s MiCA regulation, which came into full force on July 1. Swapping one crypto for another generally does not trigger capital gains tax in France. The proposed changes would tax swaps into certain EU-regulated stablecoins starting Jan. France currently applies a 31.4% flat tax to crypto gains when investors cash out or spend their holdings. The distinction is critical because the proposal targets a category of stablecoins subject to EU rules, potentially incentivizing traders to use alternatives outside that category. Francois Volpoet, Chainalysis’ CEO for France, warned that the measure could undermine efforts to bring more crypto transactions into the regulated financial system. "Do we want more taxpayers to declare their assets, or a higher tax rate applied to a base that is increasingly evaded?" Volpoet said in an email to CoinDesk. He said authorities can more easily monitor regulated stablecoin transactions than trades made through decentralized finance (DeFi) platforms or self-hosted wallets. Another amendment backed by the finance committee on Oct. 9 would require French taxpayers to declare self-hosted crypto wallets holding at least €100,000 ($116,000 approximately) in assets, with fines of up to $11,600 for failing to comply.

items.article_context_en: The bank manages custody and settlement in-house via a closed-loop model, removing the need for separate crypto wallets. The service will initially be available to clients classified as professional investors, and the London-based lender said it is the first of its kind offered by an international bank in the UAE. The debut is also a global first for Standard Chartered, according to the bank, because it marks the first time it has offered cryptocurrency trading directly to wealthy clients in any market. The bank will manage custody and settlement within its own ecosystem using a closed-loop model, it said, meaning clients will not need separate cryptocurrency wallets or third-party trading platforms. The service brings together Standard Chartered’s wealth and retail banking and corporate and investment banking businesses and operates through Zodia Markets, which is backed by the bank’s SC Ventures unit. Standard Chartered said it has received licensing approval from Dubai’s Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority(VARA). The bank introduced institutional bitcoin and ether spot trading through its U.K. arm in July last year and expanded that offering to the UAE on Sept. Standard Chartered already offers eligible clients access to crypto exchange-traded funds (ETFs), structured products and over-the-counter derivatives. It plans to expand the new trading service to other markets, but did not give a timetable in the announcement. Diversified RWA stablecoins sustain 5-7% yield from real credit as crypto funding compresses to ~4%. GENIUS pushes yield off-chain; TAM grows to $4B in 3 years. items.article_summary_en: Coinbase says bitcoin should start preparing for quantum computers now, with flexible addresses, a backup quantum-proof key and a separate debate over lost coins. What if someone builds a quantum computer fast enough to crack your bitcoin wallet's security and siphon off your coins? Nasdaq-listed crypto exchange Coinbase COIN, which holds about 5% of all bitcoin in existence today for its clients, including banks, asset managers and hedge funds, has shared its thoughts on that question in a new blog post, laying out what it believes bitcoin needs to do to stay secure against a "potential future" quantum threat. A sufficiently powerful quantum computer, one that could exist by 2029, according to Google Researchers, could do just that: reverse-engineer a private key from a public key and drain holders' bitcoin wallets.
items.article_context_en: Coinbase says bitcoin should start preparing for quantum computers now, with flexible addresses, a backup quantum-proof key and a separate debate over lost coins. What if someone builds a quantum computer fast enough to crack your bitcoin wallet's security and siphon off your coins? That's on everyone's mind, since some projections suggest that such a quantum machine, though it doesn't exist today, could arrive within a few years. Nasdaq-listed crypto exchange Coinbase COIN, which holds about 5% of all bitcoin in existence today for its clients, including banks, asset managers and hedge funds, has shared its thoughts on that question in a new blog post, laying out what it believes bitcoin needs to do to stay secure against a "potential future" quantum threat. Its first point is to start preparing now, not wait for the risk to arrive, and handle the question of lost coins separately. To follow the exchange's suggestions, it helps to know how Bitcoin's locks work and how a quantum computer can break them. Think of a bitcoin wallet as a mailbox with a narrow horizontal slot at the top and a key held only by the owner. The visible slot, through which anyone can drop letters inside, is the wallet's public key. The private key, by contrast, is the physical key that unlocks the box. Kept strictly in the owner's hands, this private key is invisible to the outside world and keeps the Bitcoin in the wallet safe. When a user sends bitcoin, their wallet uses the private key to create a digital signature, a tamper-proof stamp. The network checks it against the user's public key; if it matches, the transaction is approved. The Bitcoin blockchain uses two methods, called ECDSA and Schnorr, to create and verify these digital signatures. These are extremely secure for now because current computers aren't powerful enough to crack the math behind these techniques and reverse-engineer a user's private key from its digital signature or public key.

items.article_context_en: ZEC led a broad bounce among major tokens, and Korean chipmakers snapped a five-day losing streak ahead of Thursday’s U.S. Bitcoin rose 1.5% to just under $83,900 as of Wednesday Asian morning hours. New York Fed President John Williams said he saw no need for further rate hikes in 2027, which weakened the dollar and lifted stocks across Asia. ZEC led the majors, jumping nearly 7% to about $1,270. SOL and DOGE each gained 2.5%, and ether rose 2% to about $2,520. XRP, BNB and HYPE added between 1% and 2%, while TRX lagged with a gain of less than 1%, according to CoinDesk data. Williams did say one more hike this year may be appropriate. His comments still helped the S&P 500 pare its losses on Tuesday, and S&P 500 futures rose 0.2% with the index hovering near last week’s record. Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix both rallied, snapping the five-day losing streak that had wiped out leveraged bets on chip stocks at crypto exchanges earlier this week. MSCI’s Asia Pacific equities index rose 0.7%, rebounding from two days of losses that had pushed it to its lowest close since August. Chip-equipment maker ASML reports earnings on Wednesday, and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing reports on Thursday. Brent rose 0.7% to about $106 a barrel as a flare-up in Middle East attacks raised doubts over a recovery in energy shipments from the Persian Gulf. inflation report is the next test of Williams’ view. A reading cool enough to rule out that last hike would give bitcoin room to retest $85,000.

items.article_context_en: The exchange, which has over 18 million customers, is said to have handled business transactions involving restricted offshore gaming and gambling companies. Coins.ph, the largest cryptocurrency exchange in the Philippines, is facing punitive action from financial regulators at the country’s central bank, two people with knowledge of the situation said. The infractions, which are said to involve serving offshore gambling firms, are serious enough for the 12-year-old company to be stripped of its license to operate, which would cause “an earthquake” in the Philippines’ crypto ecosystem, according to one of the people. The exchange, which has over 18 million customers, has a 24-hour spot trading volume of about $50 million and controls some 75%-80% of peso-to-stablecoin liquidity in the Philippines, a key transaction in the world's fourth-largest remittance recipient. More than 10.8 million Filipinos live outside the country, according to the Commission on Filipinos Overseas, though most use banks and money transfer services to repatriate their earnings, some $43 billion a year. At the start of this month, Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) reportedly imposed restrictions on deposits to the exchange made through Coins.ph’s main wallet firm, DCPay Philippines. The restrictions follow the departure of several high-profile compliance staffers, including chief compliance officer Lexi Herrera, the head of anti-money laundering (AML) transaction monitoring Chris Beaño and money laundering reporting officer Irish Calagui. Coins.ph said it is aware of recent news reports about its operations, including claims about offshore gaming transactions and its engagement with the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas, in a statement shared with Coindesk after the publication of this article. The exchange said users’ funds are safe, and the firm continues to operate as a BSP licensed institution and expects to fully restore affected services soon. “Coins.ph firmly denies any claim that it knowingly serves offshore gaming or gambling operators. We hold ourselves to the requirements and standards of the BSP, AMLC and other regulatory authorities, and full compliance sits at the core of how we operate,” Coins.ph said in the emailed statement. “We value the media’s role in keeping the public informed and welcome the opportunity to share our perspective. We remain open to engaging with journalists and providing accurate information about Coins.ph,” it said. The Philippines central bank had not responded to requests for comment by publication time.

Bitcoin treasury company Strive ASST on Tuesday evening announced a new perpetual preferred stock, SATS, with a 15% fixed dividend. The company is aiming to sell 5 million shares at $100 per share, for a capital raise of $500 million, with proceeds to be used to purchase additional bitcoin BTC$83 478,64, acquire income-producing assets, or buy back stock. The new share class will sit junior to Strive’s current perpetual preferred, SATA, which has a variable rate (currently 13%). At closing of the offering, the company intends to establish a dividend reserve equal to the first 18 months of dividend payments on SATS. Unlike most bitcoin treasury companies, including far larger peer Strategy, Strive has in recent weeks been able to significantly increase its bitcoin holdings. The company last week acquired 3,311 bitcoin, bringing total holdings to 32,773 coins, currently worth about $2.7 billiion. Three months ago, holdings were below 20,000 coins. MNX, a new crypto exchange developed by former Manifold executives, went live on Tuesday offering futures contracts tied to OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek and Moonshot. items.article_context_en: MNX is offering a different way to trade the future valuations of private AI companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic and DeepSeek. A new cryptocurrency exchange will allow investors to speculate on the valuations of private artificial intelligence (AI) giants like OpenAI and Anthropic when they go public. MNX, a new crypto exchange developed by former Manifold executives, went live on Tuesday offering futures contracts tied to OpenAI, Anthropic, DeepSeek and Moonshot. The platform, built on MegaETH blockchain, raised $6.4 million from investors led by Village Global in June. Larger crypto exchanges, including OKX and Bitget, already offer contracts that let traders bet on the value of private AI companies without owning their shares. Unlike Bitget’s perpetual futures which never expire, MNX offers contracts with expiration dates at the end of 2027 and incur no recurring funding fees. OKX also offers contracts with no expiration dates, but uses a different funding mechanism. The investment is a bet that financial markets have yet to catch up with the enormous amounts of money flowing into artificial intelligence, according to Village Global. "AI is driving one of the largest investment cycles in history, despite the financial infrastructure around it remaining quite underdeveloped," said Max Killberg of Village Global. He said the firm sees an opportunity to develop financial markets around AI, rather than simply back another prediction market. Manifold Markets co-founder Stephen Gruggett told CoinDesk that MNX’s approach is better suited to private companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic, whose shares trade infrequently and are difficult to price. "OpenAI, Anthropic secondaries are illiquid and hard to price," he said. "A perp based on an illiquid, stale price is worse than meaningless: it doesn't behave the way investors expect; it's easy to manipulate; and it may have a very high and unpredictable funding rate." Traders can also use up to three times their available funds, increasing both potential profits and losses. Prices are determined by trading activity on MNX rather than an external price feed.

The trader shared a Solana wallet address on blockchain explorer Solscan to substantiate his account, though there has yet been no corresponding confirmation from the police or other authorities regarding the incident. and do crypto get the f**k out,” he posted. The incident follows recent reports of a similar U.K. robbery last December, where masked attackers beat a cryptocurrency investor with hammers and threatened to kill his pregnant wife unless he transferred hundreds of thousands of pounds in crypto. Such crimes, commonly called “wrench attacks,” involve physical violence or threats to compel crypto holders to surrender their assets. Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis estimates criminals stole more than $30 million through violent attacks in the first half of 2026. Home invasions accounted for 37% of recorded incidents, up from 14% a year earlier. France emerged as a hotspot for wrench attacks, with Chainalysis documenting at least 30 recorded incidents in the first half of this year. Blockchain security firm Certik identified 52 verified attacks globally during that period, of which 33 were in France. The figures suggest physical coercion is becoming an increasingly significant concern alongside wholly digital threats such as hacks, phishing and smart-contract exploits. The implications for investors extend beyond protecting private keys to keeping holdings confidential, limiting public disclosures about one’s trading activity and separating readily available funds from long-term reserves.

items.article_summary_en: South Korea’s FIU approved measures blocking domestic web access to 27 unregistered crypto exchanges. Websites operated from overseas will be blocked, while those operating domestically face service termination, the FIU noted. The move closes another route for South Korean investors to access unregistered exchanges after authorities restricted access to their mobile apps on Google and Apple last year. South Korean investors have been gradually moving large amounts of crypto overseas for months due to stricter rules, with an estimated $110 billion leaving domestic exchanges in 2025.
items.article_context_en: South Korea’s FIU approved measures blocking domestic web access to 27 unregistered crypto exchanges. The country’s Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU) announced Tuesday that the Korea Communications Standards Commission approved the restrictions following reviews on Oct. Websites operated from overseas will be blocked, while those operating domestically face service termination, the FIU noted. The move closes another route for South Korean investors to access unregistered exchanges after authorities restricted access to their mobile apps on Google and Apple last year. Regulators can now seek website blocks as soon as they detect unregistered activity, without waiting for a court ruling or evidence that customers have lost money. The FIU did not specify how long the restrictions will last or set a deadline for the exchanges to register. However, any exchange that wants to legally operate in the country and serve South Korean customers must register with the FIU and meet the country’s security and anti-money laundering (AML) requirements. “We respect applicable laws and regulations across jurisdictions and continuously strengthen our compliance framework in response to evolving regulatory requirements,” a KuCoin spokesperson said. “User assets remain safe and secure, and we will communicate any further updates through our official channels.” BitMart, Phemex and MEXC did not immediately respond to a CoinDesk request for comment. South Korea's proposed Digital Asset Basic Law, yet to come into force, would set the groundwork for a legal framework for digital assets, including issuance, trading, custody and supervision. The country’s Financial Services Commission and Financial Supervisory service announced new rules in April, removing the discretion exchanges had to let users bypass holding periods. The FIU said it has referred 44 unregistered operators to investigators and will seek further blocks against websites that reopen under different addresses. Only 28 virtual asset service providers are currently registered with the regulator. The financial watchdog also warned that traders using unauthorized platforms could face difficulties recovering their funds.

items.article_context_en: 13, 2026 While major cryptocurrencies remain choppy, STX, the native token of the Bitcoin layer-2 project Stacks, is rallying. The cryptocurrency has surged nearly 10% in 24 hours, 14% over the past week and more than 50% in four weeks, outperforming bitcoin BTC$83,478.64, ether ETH$2,504.88, XRP (XRP) and other cryptocurrencies. The outperformance likely reflects investor interest in Stacks’ non-custodial bitcoin staking architecture. This framework lets BTC holders stake and earn yield directly on the main Bitcoin blockchain while retaining strict control of their private keys. In contrast, traditional frameworks require users to wrap their assets into synthetic tokens (like wBTC) or move funds over cross-chain bridges to earn additional yield. Stacks’ framework relies on a mechanism called "bonding," which requires participants to lock up assets to secure the network. The "Bonding Period 3,” due in November, requires participants holding native STX to lock a specific ratio of STX alongside their BTC — equivalent to roughly 5% of the total value of their BTC — to successfully secure protocol stacking capacity. This creates a positive feedback loop for STX: As more BTC moves into the Stacks ecosystem, a larger portion of STX is systematically locked up and removed from the active market. By tying bitcoin liquidity directly to STX scarcity, the architecture skews demand-supply dynamics heavily in favor of long-term price appreciation. Period 3 follows Periods 1 and 2, which served as preparatory phases to safely transition signers and bootstrap initial liquidity. STX is not the only coin to have surged over 24 hours. BDX, REDNER, and PYTH are other major gainers, adding 6% each. It’s a sign of liquidity increasingly pivoting to coins other than the major cryptocurrencies. Still, the broader context remains tightly bound to macroeconomic indicators.
